708569.t: Perhaps related to μαδάω (madáō, “to be moist”). If so, then from Proto-Indo-European *meh₂d- (“wet; glossy; fat; well-fed”).

708593.t: Controversial: * Traditionally linked to μάχομαι (mákhomai, “to fight”); compare μάχη (mákhē, “a battle, a strife”).

708527.t: Often assigned to Proto-Indo-European *(s)mer- (“to fall into thinking, remember, care for”), which is acknowledged by Beekes, but he finds it unconvincing and instead derives it from Pre-Greek based on the ending of the word.

708522.t: The word is most probably Pre-Greek, because of its variants.

708566.t: From *μαστιγϳ- (*măstĭgj-, stem of μάστιξ) + -όω (-óō, causative/factitive verbal suffix).
